### M182. The headline VIR result (146 -> 73 classes, FS_001 = 1,197) comes from the local CPU branch, while the platform GPU run gave 76 classes and FS_001 = 812 — undercutting "strict reproducibility"
- **Lines:** L61, L72, L168, L245, L252  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-overclaims  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** Abstract L61: "collapsing 146 fragmented P. vivax antigen subfamilies into 73 globally shared structural classes on remote GPUs"; L252: "On the reference CPU baseline, Foldseek collapsed 2,592 VIR proteins ... into 73 structural classes ... Executing the same ProstT5-Foldseek tool on an ACCESS-CI NVIDIA A100 GPU produced 76 structural classes (FS_001 = 812 proteins, 336 sub-cluster representatives)".
- **Evidence:** L252 and Methods L367 record both branches (local: 73 clusters, FS_001 = 1,197; GPU: 76 clusters, FS_001 = 812). Downstream microsynteny also diverges strongly: "only eleven (three on the GPU branch) maintained conserved flanking microsynteny" (L252). The markdown mirror omits the GPU branch entirely (manuscript_v2.md L168 reports only 73 classes / 1,197 proteins and drops the discrepancy).
- **Problem:** The Abstract attributes the 73-class result to "remote GPUs" when 73 is the local CPU number; the platform run produced a different answer (FS_001 differs by 32%, microsynteny hits by 3.7x). This is the clearest internal counterexample to "unites the speed of autonomous agents with strict reproducibility" (L61) and to presenting the plane as the authoritative execution venue. The md mirror's omission looks like selective reporting.
- **Fix:** Correct the Abstract to state the result came from the verified CPU reference branch; report both branch numbers wherever the 73/1,197 figures appear; quantify how much of the biological conclusion is branch-invariant (the 97.3% cross-continental figure, p = 0.55) versus branch-dependent; and restore the GPU/CPU discrepancy to manuscript_v2.md.

### M183. Abstract escalates a provenance ambiguity in Paper2Agent into "errors"
- **Lines:** L61, L220, L222, L166  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-overclaims  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** Abstract L61: "on-graph provenance uncovers unstated statistical pooling, post-processing rules, and errors in the recent Nature Paper2Agent study."
- **Evidence:** Results describe the same observation as an ambiguity, not an error: L222 "Inspecting the published assets uncovered a critical provenance ambiguity: the analysis in Extended Data Figure 1c of Miao et al. did not derive from the full Zenodo Dataset 15 archive ... but instead utilized an unannotated 1,000-cell tutorial subset bundled with the software repository". Table 1 L166 says "Uncovers that a published Paper2Agent benchmark ran on an unannotated 1,000-cell tutorial subset". The reproduction matched that subset's published figure (L233, r = 1.0000 vs local).
- **Problem:** Using a bundled tutorial subset for an illustrative Extended Data panel is a documentation/provenance gap, not a demonstrated error in Miao et al.'s results — and the manuscript's own reproduction confirms their numbers on that subset. The authors of Paper2Agent would have a legitimate correction request against the Abstract wording.
- **Fix:** Change "errors" to "an undocumented input-data provenance gap" in the Abstract, and state that the published panel itself was reproduced faithfully once the correct input was identified.

### M184. "Unites the speed of autonomous agents with strict reproducibility" is asserted without any repeated agent runs
- **Lines:** L61, L72, L90  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-overclaims  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L61: "Our system unites the speed of autonomous agents with strict reproducibility"; L72: "every analytical step, containerized tool, and intermediate dataset is documented as an immutable history".
- **Evidence:** Each platform investigation is a single agent session (one history/workflow per study, Supplementary Tables S3--S6). The only repeat-run evidence in the workspace is in the spatial study, and it tests the TISSUE algorithm's seeds, not agent behaviour (/Users/anton/git/spatTrOrbit/notebook.md L110-120: "we executed 5 runs with distinct seeds" of the deterministic SpaGE/TISSUE pipeline). The agent planning experiment itself shows 18 distinct plans from 30 identical prompts, and the paper's own GPU-vs-CPU VIR branches disagree.
- **Problem:** What the platform makes reproducible is re-execution of a recorded workflow, not the agent's construction of it. Conflating the two overstates the contribution; a reviewer will ask "what happens if you run the same prompt into Orbit five times?" and the manuscript has no answer.
- **Fix:** Distinguish re-executability of the recorded analysis from reproducibility of the agent's decisions; state that agent trajectories were not replicated (n = 1 per study) and report at least one multi-replicate agent run on the platform to quantify trajectory variability.

### M185. Galaxy histories are not "immutable"; provenance is not "guaranteed by default"
- **Lines:** L68, L70, L112  ·  **Status:** CONFIRMED  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-overclaims  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L68: "formalized into an immutable, shareable record"; L70: "recorded within an immutable directed acyclic graph"; L112: "preserving an immutable directed acyclic graph with permanent computational provenance"; L103: "Pushing computation to public infrastructure guarantees provenance by default".
- **Evidence:** Galaxy users can delete and purge datasets and histories, rename/annotate them, upload arbitrary files as if they were tool outputs, and run tools whose provenance is a user-authored UDT that can be edited or deactivated — the manuscript itself records deactivating a UDT version mid-study ("The intermediate 3.2.1 definition created during this repair was deactivated", /Users/anton/git/beast-chrom/notebook.md L815) and swapping a prototype UDT for MACS2 (L204). Public-instance quota policies also purge data; no retention guarantee is cited.
- **Problem:** "Immutable" and "guarantees" are strong technical words with cryptographic connotations (no hashes, signatures or content-addressing are described anywhere). The accurate claim is append-only-by-default, user-purgeable, server-retained provenance.
- **Fix:** Make these replacements: - L68: "immutable, shareable record" -> "persistent, shareable record". - L70 and L112: "immutable directed acyclic graph (with permanent computational provenance)" -> "automatically recorded, append-only provenance graph". - L72: "documented as an immutable history" -> "documented as a public Galaxy history". - L103: "guarantees provenance by default ... permanent record" -> "records provenance by default ... persistent record". - L137, L173, L235, L254, L274, L532: "permanently archived/accessible" -> "publicly archived/accessible". - L260: either drop "byte-level", or report SHA-256 checksums of the archived XML files.  In the Discussion or Methods, add one sentence stating that: - histories and datasets remain user-deletable and purgeable and are subject to the instance's retention policy; - UDT definitions are versioned by UUID but can be deactivated by their owner; - long-term preservation needs export (e.g., RO-Crate/history archive to Zenodo with DOI), which the authors should state whether they did.

### M186. "Installing agent harnesses on shared supercomputers violates facility security policies" is asserted without any citation
- **Lines:** L68  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-overclaims  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L68: "Installing autonomous agent harnesses directly onto shared institutional supercomputers violates facility security policies and remains administratively unsustainable."
- **Evidence:** No citation is attached; no acceptable-use policy, facility statement, or survey is cited anywhere in the manuscript. This sentence carries a load-bearing part of the motivation for the whole architecture, and it is also in tension with L116's softer framing ("Researchers never have to negotiate agentic shell or head-node access").
- **Problem:** Many ACCESS-CI and institutional facilities permit user-space installation of software, including LLM clients, in home/project space; the blanket policy claim is checkable and likely wrong in general. A referee will ask for the policy text.

### M189. "Matched the published DEG counts within 0.3--0.9%" understates the actual 0.3--1.3% range
- **Lines:** L181, L187  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-overclaims  ·  **Confidence:** high

### M190. "Proving that the authors fitted one pooled model" overstates an inference from identical baseMean values
- **Lines:** L181, L156  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-overclaims  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L181: "every gene carried a single identical \texttt{baseMean} value across all four contrasts, proving that the authors fitted one pooled 30-sample five-level factor model rather than four pairwise models"; Table 1 L156 repeats "proves that the authors fitted one pooled 30-sample model".
- **Evidence:** The evidence is a signature consistent with pooling (identical baseMean plus recovered standard errors "to four decimal places", L181). The original authors were not contacted, and no author confirmation is cited.
- **Problem:** Identical baseMean is strong circumstantial evidence, not proof; alternative explanations (baseMean recomputed once from the full matrix and pasted across tabs) exist. "Proving" what another group did, in print, without their confirmation is exactly the sort of statement an aggrieved author would contest.
- **Fix:** Use "indicating" or "consistent only with"; add the strongest supporting evidence (SE agreement to 4 dp) as the basis, and state that the inference was not confirmed by the original authors (or confirm it with them).

### M191. Coverage 8--9 points above nominal is described as "well-calibrated"/"conservative" without noting intervals are too wide
- **Lines:** L233, L235, L228  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-overclaims  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L233: "Empirical coverage reached 86.46\% at nominal 77\% coverage"; L235: "Conformal coverage remained well-calibrated at 85.61\%"; L235: "confirmed conservative coverage bounds".
- **Evidence:** Nominal 1 - alpha = 0.77 (Methods L364); observed 86.46% (subset) and 85.61% (full). The 10-fold CV results are closer (79.05% at 77%, 81.33% at 80%, L235).
- **Problem:** Exceeding nominal coverage by ~9 points means the prediction intervals are over-wide, i.e. mis-calibrated in the conservative direction and less informative — not "well-calibrated". Since uncertainty quantification is the scientific point of the TISSUE reproduction, the framing matters.
- **Fix:** Report the coverage gap explicitly and describe it as conservative mis-calibration (over-wide intervals), noting that the 10-fold CV coverage is much closer to nominal; avoid "well-calibrated" for the single-gene runs.

### M192. A non-significant permutation test (p = 0.55) is used as positive evidence for pre-dispersal diversification
- **Lines:** L246, L252, L239  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-overclaims  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L246: "A quantitative tip-label parsimony permutation test confirms that observed character transitions (score = 160) are indistinguishable from 1,000 random shuffles (null mean: 159.2 +/- 3.8, p = 0.55). These results demonstrate that the VIR structural scaffold diversified prior to continental separation and is maintained across lineages by subtelomeric ectopic recombination." L252: "Repertoire diversification predated continental separation."
- **Evidence:** The test statistic equals the null mean (160 vs 159.2 +/- 3.8); the data are consistent with the null of no geographic structure, i.e. the test has simply failed to reject. No power analysis, no alternative-model comparison (e.g. explicit dating of the structural radiation), and no molecular-clock estimate of the radiation relative to human dispersal is presented.
- **Problem:** Failure to reject a null is not evidence for a specific historical scenario, and the mechanistic claim about "subtelomeric ectopic recombination" maintaining the core is asserted from a correlation (64.5% of loci subtelomeric) with no recombination inference. An author of the pathogen-biology literature would reject "demonstrate" outright.
- **Fix:** Rewrite as "we detect no geographic signal in the structural phylogeny (p = 0.55), which is consistent with — but does not establish — diversification prior to continental separation"; add power/sensitivity analysis or an explicit dated comparison if the stronger claim is to be kept, and label the recombination mechanism as a hypothesis.

### M197. The either_frac = 0.851 overlap rule is a one-parameter grid search fitted to the published totals, then reported as agreement "within 0.4–4.6%"; the cross-tissue test shows it does not transfer
- **Lines:** L190, L210, L162  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-stats  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L210: "A systematic grid search showed that a near-containment rule (\texttt{either\_frac} $= 0.851$ ...) reproduced the published totals (44,780 midgut and 67,594 salivary-gland regions) along with downstream assigned genes, promoters, and candidate enhancers within 0.4--4.6\%"; caption L190 repeats this as quantitative validation.
- **Evidence:** Published targets 43,010 and 68,576 vs fitted 44,780 (+4.12%) and 67,594 (−1.43%); the threshold was selected by searching over either_frac against exactly those targets. The manuscript's own cross-fit (L210) gives 0.884 in midgut and 0.821 in salivary glands — a ±4% spread around the pooled 0.851 — and no uncertainty, CI, or null distribution is given for the grid search over a continuous parameter.
- **Problem:** Agreement computed at the parameter value chosen to maximise agreement is circular: the 0.4–4.6% figures are residuals of a fit, not an independent validation, yet Figure 3D and Table 1 present them alongside the genuinely unfitted 90.7–93.2% coordinate recovery. The divergent single-tissue optima are evidence that the recovered 'rule' is not a single unstated counting step.
- **Fix:** Report the grid-search profile (agreement vs either_frac) and the width of the near-optimal plateau, state degrees of freedom consumed, and present the cross-tissue optima as falsifying evidence: conclude only that 'some near-containment rule' explains the totals, not that either_frac = 0.851 is the authors' rule. Keep the fitted and unfitted numbers in separate panels/rows.

### M198. 1,784/943/854 DEGs claimed from a pseudobulk design with only 2 biological replicates and ~2 residual degrees of freedom, with Louvain resolution tuned per replicate
- **Lines:** L216, L361  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-stats  ·  **Confidence:** medium
- **Claim:** L216: "Sample-blocked pseudobulk differential expression in edgeR (\texttt{\textasciitilde 0 + coarse\_label + sample\_id}) across 8,248 filtered genes identified 1,784 differentially expressed genes ... ($\text{FDR} \le 0.05$)"; same line: "3,836 cells in \texttt{SRR26591148} at Louvain resolution 0.25, and 2,871 cells in \texttt{SRR26591149} at Louvain resolution 0.75".
- **Evidence:** The design has 3 coarse labels × 2 samples = 6 pseudobulk libraries; with ~0 + coarse_label + sample_id this leaves ≈2 residual degrees of freedom for dispersion estimation. Cluster sizes for the minority populations are 73 and 213 cells (HC-like) and 257 and 75 cells (VM-like) — i.e. the pseudobulk 'replicates' for those labels differ by ~3×. Choosing a different Louvain resolution per replicate (0.25 vs 0.75) is an analyst degree of freedom applied downstream of the comparison.
- **Problem:** Two biological replicates give almost no information about between-sample variance, so edgeR FDR values here are strongly model-dependent; and the cluster definitions on which the contrasts rest were obtained with per-replicate tuning, which is the same researcher-degrees-of-freedom problem the manuscript criticises in reanalysed studies.
- **Fix:** State the residual df and that DEG counts at n = 2 are indicative only; report the criterion used to pick each replicate's Louvain resolution (and a sensitivity analysis across resolutions showing DEG counts); prefer reporting marker-gene ranks (which the paper already does, and which are robust) over absolute DEG counts.

### M199. A non-significant permutation test (p = 0.55) is interpreted as positive evidence that diversification predated continental separation
- **Lines:** L246, L252  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-stats  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L246: "A quantitative tip-label parsimony permutation test confirms that observed character transitions (score = 160) are indistinguishable from 1,000 random shuffles (null mean: $159.2 \pm 3.8$, $p = 0.55$). These results demonstrate that the VIR structural scaffold diversified prior to continental separation"; L252 repeats "Repertoire diversification predated continental separation."
- **Evidence:** Observed score 160 vs null 159.2 ± 3.8 — the observed value sits 0.2 SD above the null mean, i.e. the data are uninformative about geographic structure on this tree. No power analysis is reported, and the test is applied to 338 FS_001 representatives only.
- **Problem:** Failure to reject a null of random tip-label assignment is absence of evidence, not evidence of ancestral pre-dispersal diversification; with 338 tips and a permutation SD of 3.8 the test may well lack power to detect moderate geographic clustering. The manuscript converts a null result into a positive historical-biogeographic claim.
- **Fix:** State the result as 'no detectable geographic signal' and add a power/equivalence analysis (e.g. simulate the parsimony score under lineage-specific radiation scenarios to show which effect sizes would have been detected), or support the pre-dispersal claim with a dated/ancestral-state reconstruction rather than a non-significant permutation.

### M200. A second deterministic run of the same 42 cohorts moves t_MRCA by >10 years in 14 cohorts (up to 3,268 years); this run-to-run instability is nowhere reported
- **Lines:** L262, L272, L170  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-stats  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L262: "All 42 reference cohorts completed successfully ... median core algorithmic execution time of 3.41 seconds per study"; L272 reports a single-run concordance taxonomy as if the estimates were stable.
- **Evidence:** /Users/anton/git/beast-chrom/deterministic_benchmark_results.tsv compares `reproduction_tmrca` with `run1_tmrca` for the same cohorts: median |Δ| = 1.32 yr, 22/41 cohorts differ by >1 yr, 14/41 by >10 yr — 37_measles 1700.82 → −1566.94 (Δ 3,268 yr), 20_avian_influenza_n7 1787.22 → 1174.90 (Δ 612 yr), 18_lassa 1931.67 → 1385.03 (Δ 547 yr), 30_mpox 1967.29 → 2024.29 (Δ 57 yr), and even the headline Ebola cohort 00_ebola_sierraleone 2014.23 → 2004.92 (Δ 9.3 yr). The differences track a change of `active_model` (OLS/SPLINE/PGLS) selected per run.
- **Problem:** The reported point estimates and the concordance taxonomy are conditional on an unreported, data-driven model-selection step whose outcome is unstable; the headline Ebola result that the manuscript quotes (2014.23) flips to 2004.92 in the repository's own deterministic rerun. No selection uncertainty, model-selection penalty, or run-to-run variance is propagated into the Fieller intervals.
- **Fix:** Report the model-selection procedure and its criterion explicitly, report both runs (or an ensemble over OLS/SPLINE/PGLS) with selection uncertainty folded into the interval, and state the run-to-run |Δ| distribution; alternatively pre-register one model per cohort before looking at the BEAST comparator.

### M201. "3.41 seconds per study" versus "weeks of Bayesian MCMC" compares core algorithm time against end-to-end MCMC, and no timing data exists in the repository

### M206. 'Immutable' histories and 'permanent' provenance contradict UseGalaxy.org storage and terms
- **Lines:** L68, L70, L72, L112, L137, L173, L235, L254, L274, L532  ·  **Status:** CONFIRMED  ·  **Auditor:** gap-access-ci-compute-routing  ·  **Confidence:** high

At L68, L70 and L112, replace "immutable DAG/record" with "a recorded provenance graph in which each job's tool version, parameters and inputs are fixed once executed". 3. At L137, L173, L235, L254, L274 and L532, replace "permanently archived/accessible on UseGalaxy.org" with "publicly accessible on UseGalaxy.org". 4. Export each cited history (Galaxy history export / RO-Crate) and each workflow, deposit them in Zenodo (histories) and WorkflowHub (workflows), and cite the DOIs in Supplementary Tables case2/case3 as the archival record. 5. Add one Methods sentence on UseGalaxy.org storage: it is not backed up, it may archive inactive data, and it has no retention SLA. Say that the DOI deposits are the durable copies.
- **Verifier:** CONFIRMED: I checked the external record myself and it matches what the finder reported. The finder cited the wrong line in one place: L72 does not say "documented as an immutable history". grep finds neither "immutable" nor "permanen" nor "archiv" on that line. The manuscript also offers no archival backstop. grep finds no WorkflowHub, RO-Crate or DOI for any history or workflow; "Zenodo" appears only for the input Dataset 15. The claims carry weight because reproducibility is the paper's core selling point. Severity stays MAJOR rather than CRITICAL: this is an over …

### M207. Vendor-agnostic and local-model claims are untested; no Orbit case study names the LLM it used
- **Lines:** L70, L109, L143-L145, L177-L275  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-architecture  ·  **Confidence:** high

Model names appear only in the local benchmark (L84, L294, L327). Pi.dev does list Ollama (https://pi.dev), but no local or open-weight model was run on any reported analysis. Loom exec-guard/model-tier.ts classifies any id containing 'flash', 'mini', 'haiku', etc. as 'weak' and converts asks to denies, so behavior differs by model. In the authors' C. auris tests, the weaker models failed (haiku 0/1).
- **Problem:** The results cannot be reproduced without the model identity and version. 'Vendor-agnostic' is a property of the interface, not something these experiments demonstrate, since all evidence comes from commercial frontier models.
- **Fix:** For every case study, report harness, model ID and version, date, human-turn count and LLM cost. Either evaluate at least one open-weight or local model end-to-end, or restrict the claim to 'supports'.

### M220. Execution guard is described as stricter than the code
- **Lines:** L345  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-architecture  ·  **Confidence:** high

### M35. '60-step' counts input steps and plumbing; the workflow was not compiled 'directly' from the methods text
- **Lines:** L156, L176  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** gap-hokken-workflow-scale  ·  **Confidence:** high

Of the 48 tool steps, 20 are collection or parameter plumbing: 5 __APPLY_RULES__, 8 __EXTRACT_DATASET__, 2 __BUILD_LIST__, 1 __FLATTEN__ and 4 compose_text_param. The final workflow came out of a long repair loop: open-requirements.ledger.yml has 48 resolved and 17 open entries, and the deg-shortfall plan records repeated rebuilds (6f392105ef0218a7, then e051decbd001773e, then b3638784a5d2aa43). The pooled-model fix came from post-hoc investigation, not from the methods text.
- **Problem:** Read literally, '60-step compiled directly from methods text' overstates both how much analysis the workflow does and how automatic its construction was.
- **Fix:** Report it as '60 steps (12 inputs, 48 tool steps)' and say that the final workflow followed iterative, ledger-tracked repair after the initial compilation.

### M56. Pseudocount placement and pipeline details differ from the paper's stated chain
- **Lines:** L204, L189, L357  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** toenhake  ·  **Confidence:** medium
- **Claim:** L204: "scores Poisson q-values via bdgcmp -m qpois against a genomic DNA control with a 0.1 pseudocount"; "omitted the 0.1 control pseudocount"; L189: "raw genomic DNA control pileups (plus a 0.1 pseudocount scaled per million reads)".
- **Evidence:** Toenhake STAR Methods: "The pileup tracks of the binned libraries were then summed, scaled per million of reads and a pseudocount of 0.1 was added to every position. Regions of local enrichment were identified with macs2 bdgcmp using the gDNA pileup track as background and scored in qvalues (-m qpois). ... bgpeakcall ... (-c 3.0) ... (-g 150) ... (-l 100)". The pseudocount is stated for the ATAC libraries, not explicitly for the gDNA control. The paper also bins libraries by insert size in 5 bp steps, uses --extsize = half the mean insert size, applies a +4/−5 Tn5 shift, and uses replicate 1 only for downstream analyses. It cites 'MACS2 release 2.7', not 2.2.9.1.
- **Problem:** The flags -m qpois, -c 3, -l 100 and -g 150 are accurate. However, the manuscript's root-cause story rests on a 'control pseudocount' the paper does not explicitly describe. 'raw ... pileups ... scaled per million' in L189/L357 is self-contradictory. The version change (2.7 → 2.2.9.1) and the binning, extsize and replicate choices are not disclosed.
- **Fix:** Quote the paper's pseudocount wording accurately: pseudocount added to the scaled pileups, with control handling as implemented. Drop 'raw' from L189/L357. Note the MACS2 version difference and which ATAC replicate was used.

### M81. Vyklicka et al. is dated 2026 but was published 10 December 2025

- **Problem:** The volume is 16 (the 2026 volume) but the publication year is 2025; both the in-text "(Sci Rep 2026)" and the bib year are wrong, and the DOI stem (s41598-025-) confirms 2025.
- **Fix:** Set year = 2025 in references.bib (keep volume 16, article 1917) and change the caption to "Sci Rep 2025"; the citation key may stay.

### M82. "The published significance threshold (padj < 0.01)" misstates Vyklicka et al.'s DEG threshold
- **Lines:** L137  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** char-pathogen  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** "$p_{adj}$ = 2.99 \times 10^{-3}$), which reproduces the published significance threshold ($p_{adj} < 0.01$)"
- **Evidence:** Vyklicka et al. Methods: "genes with an adjusted p-value (padj) < 0.05 were considered significantly differentially expressed"; Fig. 4 legend: padj <= 0.05 (*), padj <= 0.01 (**).
- **Problem:** padj < 0.01 is the paper's ** display tier, not its significance threshold, which is 0.05. As phrased it implies a stricter study-wide criterion than the authors used.
- **Fix:** Rephrase to "clears the ** tier (padj <= 0.01) of the published figure; the study's DEG threshold was padj < 0.05".

### M83. "Proves/proving" the authors' model design overstates what identical baseMean values and matched standard errors can establish
- **Lines:** L156, L181  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-authors  ·  **Confidence:** medium
- **Claim:** L156 (Table 1): "proves that the authors fitted one pooled 30-sample model rather than pairwise contrasts"; L181: "every gene carried a single identical \texttt{baseMean} value across all four contrasts, proving that the authors fitted one pooled 30-sample five-level factor model".
- **Evidence:** Hokken et al. state only "Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified by DESeq2 for R by Bioconductor (BaseMean >= 30, P-value < 0.05, adjusted P-value < 0.1, log2FC > 1 or < -1)" and that comparisons were "between the samples taken without the addition of itraconazole (t = 0) and the samples incubated with itraconazole at the different time points" (PMC6327609) — a single-dataset design is the natural reading, not a concealed choice.
- **Problem:** Identical baseMean shows all samples sat in one DESeqDataSet; the specific "five-level factor" parameterisation and isolate handling remain inferred. Combined with the abstract's "uncovers unstated statistical pooling", the framing implies the authors omitted something improper when their design is conventional and partially stated.
- **Fix:** "...indicating that the published results come from a single DESeq2 dataset spanning all 30 libraries rather than four independent pairwise fits; refitting that way reproduced the published standard errors to four decimal places and the DEG counts within 0.3-0.9%." Replace "unstated statistical pooling" in the abstract with "design details recoverable only by refitting".

For example: "...reproduced the temporal enrichment inversion: 135 up- vs. 2 down-regulated [aspect] terms at 30 min (published: 194 vs. 5 biological-process terms before redundancy removal) and 0 up- vs. 136 down-regulated terms at 240 min (published: no up-regulated terms; down-regulated counts not reported)." Name the GO aspect(s), the GO annotation snapshot and date, the p/FDR cutoffs, and whether the counts come before or after the Jaccard redundancy reduction. Note that absolute counts are not directly comparable because the original AspGD annotation and REVIGO filters are no longer available. Add the source file or Galaxy dataset IDs for the 135/2/136 counts to Supplementary Table tab:brc_artifacts.
- **Verifier:** CONFIRMED: The core fact holds. I re-fetched Hokken et al. 2019, BMC Genomics 20:28 (PMC6327609). The only enriched-term counts it gives are for 30 min: 194 terms for the up-regulated genes and 5 for the down-regulated genes, both in the biological-process category and both counted "before the removal of redundant terms". For 120 and 240 min it says only that "no enriched terms were found in the up-regulated genes". It gives no number of down-regulated terms at 240 min, so the manuscript's 136 has nothing published to compare against. L181 reports 135/2 and 0/136 with no published comparator, and I found no file in /Users/anton/git that backs 135 or 136. However, the finder's "-30% and -60%" …

### M87. Toenhake peak-calling reconstruction adds a fragment-size filter and a merge step not in the published chain
- **Lines:** L202, L357  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** char-pathogen  ·  **Confidence:** medium
- **Claim:** "quantified accessibility across all eight fragment-filtered ATAC-seq alignments"; Methods: "Fragment-filtered ATAC-seq alignments ($\le 100$~bp) were scored against raw genomic DNA control pileups ... Called peaks were merged across timepoints (\texttt{bedtools MergeBed -d 100})"
- **Evidence:** Toenhake et al. 2018, Cell Host Microbe 23:557 (PMC5899830), Methods: libraries were "binned ... based on the insert size in steps of 5 bp", Tn5 +4/-5 shifted, "a pileup track for each (binned) ATAC library was calculated by MACS2 pileup with --extsize set to half the mean insert size", tracks "summed, scaled per million of reads and a pseudocount of 0.1 was added to every position", bdgcmp -m qpois against the gDNA pileup, bdgpeakcall q < 0.001 (-c 3.0) with -g 150 and -l 100; peaks across timepoints merged keeping the highest-scoring summit (4,035 merged peaks).
- **Problem:** The published chain uses insert-size binning with per-bin extsize rather than a <=100 bp fragment filter, and merging is handled inside bdgpeakcall (-g 150) plus summit selection rather than an external bedtools MergeBed -d 100. These are defensible substitutions but are presented as following "the paper's stated MACS2 chain", so a referee cannot tell which differences explain the residual 3,903 vs 4,035 gap.
- **Fix:** List the deviations from the published chain explicitly (fragment filter, external merge, MACS2 2.2.9.1 vs the authors' 2.x release) and note their effect on peak counts. The rest of the chain (qpois, 0.1 pseudocount, per-million scaling, -c 3 -l 100 -g 150, 4,035/3,755/2,118/2,771/165-of-169 published values) checks out exactly.

### M92. Salvador-I is a Sanger shotgun assembly; "short-read" is inaccurate, and the A-L/12-subfamily scheme is only loosely attributable to the two cited papers
- **Lines:** L239  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** char-ml-struct  ·  **Confidence:** medium
- **Claim:** L239: "Initial sequence-based classifications based on the incomplete, short-read Salvador-I reference defined ten to twelve subfamilies, designated VIR-A through VIR-L \cite{carlton2008, lopez2013}."
- **Evidence:** Carlton et al. 2008 (Nature 455:757-763, PMID 18843361) sequenced Salvador-I by Sanger whole-genome shotgun; Auburn et al. 2016 characterise it as "highly fragmented with over 2500 unassembled scaffolds", not short-read. López et al. 2013 (PMID 23324551) state the 346-gene/12-subfamily (A-L) scheme as pre-existing ("presently composed of 346 vir genes subdivided into 12 different subfamilies based on sequence homologies detected by BLAST") and their own result removes three subfamilies from the family.
- **Problem:** "Short-read" misdescribes the technology (fragmentation, not read length, was the limitation), and citing lopez2013 for "defined ten to twelve subfamilies" credits it with a classification it revised rather than created.
- **Fix:** Use "the fragmented Sanger-era Salvador-I reference (>2,500 scaffolds)" and attribute the 12 A-L subfamilies to the original scheme, noting that López et al. 2013 reclassified it (three subfamilies removed, unclustered genes absorbed).

### M93. The "146 artificial subfamilies" baseline is the manuscript's own MCL run at a deliberately higher inflation than the published classification, yet is presented as the prior state of the literature
- **Lines:** L239, L245, L367  ·  **Status:** CONFIRMED (originally CRITICAL)  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-authors  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L239: "Markov clustering fractures the repertoire into 146 artificial subfamilies." L245: "sequence-only Markov clustering fractures the repertoire into 146 artificial subfamilies ... The dominant superfamily, FS\_001, unifies 89 sequence subfamilies" (and L252: "89 sequence subfamilies that previous methods treated as unrelated lineages").
- **Evidence:** Methods L367 shows the 146 clusters are this paper's own baseline: "Sequence-only baseline clustering used MMseqs2 v18.8cc5c and MCL v22.282 ($I = 2.0$, 146 clusters)". ## Confounds & unfair comparisons

### M122. 'Orders of magnitude' resource differences not supported by Table S1
- **Lines:** L90  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-confounds  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L90: 'Their resource footprints varied by orders of magnitude'.
- **Evidence:** Table S1 L408-L410: RAM 2-4 GB vs 16-30 GB vs <6 GB (~8x max); disk 15-20 GB vs >100 GB vs <20 GB (~5-7x). The Claude disk figure also included a human-driven container deletion (L418).
- **Problem:** The largest spread is under one order of magnitude, from n=1 runs.
- **Fix:** Say 'varied up to ~8-fold'.

### M123. Wang scRNA-seq uses a different clustering resolution per replicate yet claims 'without any marker tuning'
- **Lines:** L164, L216  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-confounds  ·  **Confidence:** medium
- **Claim:** L216: 3,836 cells 'at Louvain resolution 0.25' and 2,871 'at Louvain resolution 0.75' ... 'Without any marker tuning ... independently recovered the primary marker genes'.
- **Evidence:** The resolutions differ 3-fold between replicates (L216). 754 cells were dropped as 'minor replicate-specific clusters'. Post-QC cells are 6,707 vs the published 7,147 (-6.2%), described as 'closely matching'.
- **Problem:** Per-replicate resolution choice plus dropping inconsistent clusters is tuning, even if marker genes were not tuned.
- **Fix:** Justify the resolutions (e.g., a stability criterion fixed in advance) or use a single resolution, and report the clustering tuning explicitly.

## Overclaims & rhetoric

### M124. "Cutting-edge discovery at scale" and "dating 42 pathogen epidemics" present re-estimation as new discovery
- **Lines:** L61, L72, L170, L256  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-overclaims  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L61: "Beyond auditing past work, the platform enables cutting-edge discovery at scale: ... and dating 42 pathogen epidemics in seconds per cohort".
- **Evidence:** The 42 cohorts are explicitly re-analyses of published benchmark XMLs: L260 "The agent compiled 42 published reference cohorts ... Original author XML files were archived"; L258 "we re-analyzed emergence dates across 42 published high-priority pathogen cohorts to determine whether tree-free manifold dating achieves numerical concordance with established Bayesian benchmarks". Table 1 L170 calls it a "production re-analysis".
- **Problem:** Re-estimating published emergence dates with a new method is method validation, not discovery, and listing it under "cutting-edge discovery" inflates the novelty budget of the Abstract. The only genuinely new biology is the single VIR analysis, whose headline number is branch-dependent (see separate finding).
- **Fix:** Restrict "discovery" to the VIR analysis and describe the 42-cohort work as a large-scale methodological benchmark/re-analysis in the Abstract and Table 1.

### M125. "Hit hardware limits" generalizes a single agent's self-inflicted disk exhaustion
- **Lines:** L61, L90, L103  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-overclaims  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L61: "In local shells, agents ... hit hardware limits"; L103 cites "the limits of local hardware"; L90: "Their resource footprints varied by orders of magnitude".
- **Evidence:** Supplementary Table S1 (L410, L418) shows only the Claude run exceeded resources (">100 GB scratch disk (49 GB Nextflow cache ...)", "Host disk exhaustion (required manual container deletion and skipping QC)"); Gemini used 15--20 GB and Codex <20 GB, both with "None" execution friction, on a 24-core / 62 GB workstation. All three completed the analysis locally, including STAR-based alignment, which L103 cites as not scaling locally.
- **Problem:** Two of three local runs met no hardware limit, so the plural generalization rests on n=1, and the one failure was caused by the agent's choice of a containerized Nextflow pipeline with caching, not by the task's intrinsic compute demand.
- **Fix:** Qualify to "one of three local agents exhausted host disk" and distinguish agent-induced resource waste from intrinsic compute requirements; reserve the scaling argument for the analyses that genuinely could not run locally (ProstT5/A100, 30-sample STAR cohorts).

### M126. Anecdotal and second-person narrative passages are unsuitable for the target venue
- **Lines:** L66, L78  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-overclaims  ·  **Confidence:** medium
- **Claim:** L66: "At our own research institutions, we have watched numerous graduate students, postdocs, and PIs (even those who are AI-averse) adopt these agentic tools, become hooked, and stop analyzing data in any other way." L78: "Suppose a student is given a task of analyzing RNA-seq data by an advisor. The student is adventurous enough to try to use one of the widely advertised agents ... (note that planning is not a widely adopted discipline in biomedical research and that appropriate use of agents requires significant changes to the present curriculum)."
- **Evidence:** No data, survey or citation supports the adoption claim or the curriculum assertion; L68's "equally thrilling and terrifying" and "the coming avalanche ... is on the way" (L281) are similarly editorial.
- **Problem:** Unsourced anecdote presented as a trend, plus a hypothetical-student vignette and a parenthetical editorial aside, weaken an otherwise empirical paper and give a referee an easy stylistic objection.
- **Fix:** Replace the anecdote with a citation (adoption survey or usage statistics) or delete it; compress the student vignette into one factual sentence motivating the planning experiment and move the curriculum remark to the Discussion.

### M127. Figure 1 caption says planning "fragmented into 18 distinct pipeline scripts" although no code was produced
- **Lines:** L84, L78  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-overclaims  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L84: "Unsupervised planning fragmented into 18 distinct pipeline scripts across the cohort."
- **Evidence:** The prompt explicitly forbade execution and code: "DO NOT perform the analysis, do not download data, do not install software. Produce ONLY a detailed analysis PLAN" (L307) and "Output the complete plan as Markdown" (L320). The underlying data file (~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/ca9cf8af-.../scratch/bacillus/choices/artifact_data.json, 30 records, 10 per family) yields exactly 18 distinct combinations over the eight plotted decisions (verified by recomputation), i.e. 18 plans, not scripts.
- **Problem:** "Pipeline scripts" misdescribes the artifact and inflates the finding by implying executable divergence in the planning experiment.
- **Fix:** Change to "18 distinct analysis plans" in the caption; keep "scripts" only for the execution experiment (26 scripts, Table S2).

### M128. The "22.5x speedup" compares two different algorithms against different references and is credited to the platform
- **Lines:** L122, L154, L334  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-overclaims  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L122: "This switch accelerated processing more than twentyfold (40 seconds vs. 15 minutes)"; Table 1 L154 lists "switching to 22.5x faster pseudoalignment" as a platform highlight.
- **Evidence:** Methods L334: Kallisto pseudoalignment against the 4.75 Mb CDS set (40 s, 12 MB output) versus HISAT2 spliced alignment against the 5.43 Mb genome plus featureCounts (15 min, 5.8 GB BAM).
- **Problem:** The speedup is an algorithm-and-reference choice available on any laptop, not an infrastructure benefit, and the human (not the agent or the platform) made the switch (L122). Presenting it in the platform-highlight column conflates three different sources of improvement.
- **Fix:** Report it as an algorithmic comparison (pseudoalignment vs spliced alignment on different references) attributable to expert steering, and remove it from the list of platform-conferred advantages.

### M129. The 42-cohort benchmark validates an unpublished method by the same senior authors, which is not flagged
- **Lines:** L258, L370  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-overclaims  ·  **Confidence:** medium
- **Claim:** L258: "we recently developed HyphAeon and its molecular-clock benchmark module ChronAeon ... \cite{pond2026hyphaeon}".
- **Evidence:** references.bib: pond2026hyphaeon is a bioRxiv preprint (2026.09.06.749597) whose author list includes the corresponding authors of this manuscript. No peer-reviewed validation of ChronAeon is cited, yet its outputs are used as the scientific payload of the platform's largest-scale demonstration.
- **Problem:** Readers cannot separate "the platform scaled a method" from "the method is correct"; the discordance in 19/42 cohorts is then attributed to BEAST priors (L272) rather than to a possible limitation of the unreviewed method, which is an unfalsifiable framing.
- **Fix:** State plainly that ChronAeon is the authors' own method under review, keep the platform claim (concurrent mapping, provenance, UDT registration) separate from the methodological claim, and present the four-category taxonomy of discordance as hypotheses rather than diagnoses.

## Statistical framing

### M130. Agent-divergence results are single-shot: 30 plans and 3 executions with no repeat runs, no sampling-temperature control, and no uncertainty on any count
- **Lines:** L78, L84, L90, L294  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-stats  ·  **Confidence:** medium
- **Claim:** L78: "The agents generated 18 proposed workflows ... eleven of these plans would produce different scientific outcomes"; L90: "the agents generated twenty-six distinct custom scripts totaling over 1,200 lines".
- **Evidence:** Methods L294 describes one prompt, ten agents per family, one execution per family on one workstation. No repeated sampling of the same agent/model, no CI on the 18/11/26 counts, and no inter-rater reliability for the manual classification of the eight decision axes. The Bacillus execution numbers in make_figure2_execution.py (L40–L97) are hard-coded with no source table in the repository.
- **Problem:** Counts of distinct plans are functions of sampling temperature and of the coder's granularity in collapsing decisions; with n = 10 per family and a single coder, the headline divergence statistics carry unquantified sampling and classification variance, and the three execution runs cannot separate model family from run-to-run chance.
- **Fix:** Report binomial CIs on the per-family decision frequencies, document the decoding parameters, have a second coder classify a subset and report agreement, and either repeat the execution runs (≥3 per family) or explicitly label the execution comparison as anecdotal.

### M131. Pearson r = 0.9622 on log2FC across "all 5,472 coding loci" is computed on 5,250 genes and is inflated by large-effect genes
- **Lines:** L131, L137, L334  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-stats  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L137/L131: "Across all 5,472 bacterial coding loci, Kallisto pseudoalignment and HISAT2 spliced alignment showed near-perfect agreement (Pearson $r = 0.9622$)"; L334 adds "$R^2 = 0.9258$".
- **Evidence:** Recomputed from /Users/anton/git/orbit-paper/bacillus-rnaseq-run/deseq2_kallisto_full_results.tsv vs deseq2_glucose_vs_control.tsv: r = 0.9622 and R² = 0.9258 reproduce exactly, but only 5,250 of 5,472 loci have log2FC in both tables (222 NA). Spearman ρ = 0.9719; restricted to baseMean > 10 (4,852 genes) r = 0.9744; mean |Δlog2FC| = 0.178; the two pipelines' FDR<0.05 gene sets (533 vs 554) share 503 genes, Jaccard = 0.861.
- **Problem:** The claim 'all 5,472 loci' overstates the denominator, and a Pearson r on log2FC is dominated by the handful of large-effect genes while the practically relevant disagreement (14% of significant calls differ between pipelines) is not reported.
- **Fix:** State n = 5,250 genes with non-missing estimates, add the Spearman ρ and mean |Δlog2FC| = 0.18, and report the concordance of the significant gene sets (503/584 shared, Jaccard 0.86) as the operational measure of equivalence.

### M132. Hokken standard-error inflation (18–26%) and the 31%/39% DEG shortfall have no supporting data anywhere in the workspace
- **Lines:** L181  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-stats  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L181: "Twelve-sample fits inflated standard errors by 18--26\%, preventing attenuated late-timepoint responses from clearing the significance threshold" and "those pairwise fits fell short of the published DEG counts by 31\% at 120 minutes and 39\% at 240 minutes, recovering only 82 of the 186 genes".
- **Evidence:** No Hokken/A. fumigatus DESeq2 output, lfcSE table, or DEG list exists in /Users/anton/git/orbit-paper or in the sibling repos (searched for 'hokken' across /Users/anton/git to depth 5: only manuscript/figures/brc_panels/hokken_fig3.png, a rendered panel). make_brc_reproductions_figure.py only tiles pre-rendered PNGs and plots no data.
- **Problem:** The claim that a pooled model was used by the original authors rests on these quantitative comparisons, none of which a referee can check; 'proving that the authors fitted one pooled 30-sample model' is also stronger than identical baseMean values warrant (identical baseMean is consistent with, but does not uniquely identify, a pooled fit).
- **Fix:** Deposit the per-timepoint lfcSE comparison and DEG lists (or link the Galaxy datasets by HID) and soften 'proving' to 'indicating'; report the SE inflation as a distribution (median and IQR over genes) rather than a bare range.

### M133. 86.46% empirical coverage at nominal 77% is a ~9.5-point miscalibration, reported as successful reproduction and "well-calibrated"
- **Lines:** L228, L233, L235  ·  **Status:** CONFIRMED (originally MAJOR)  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-stats  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L233: "Empirical coverage reached 86.46\% at nominal 77\% coverage ($\alpha = 0.23$)"; L235: "Conformal coverage remained well-calibrated at 85.61\%."
- **Evidence:** Verified from /Users/anton/git/spatTrOrbit/local_reference/galaxy_smoke_per_cell_results.csv (recomputed coverage 0.8646, n = 3,405) and full_dataset15_galaxy_summary.json (0.8561). Target is 0.77. The leak-free 10-fold CV in the same repo (notebook.md §9.2) gives 79.05% at nominal 77% — i.e. the single-gene 86.5%/85.6% numbers are not cross-validated, and Acta2-specific CV coverage is 95.54% at nominal 90% and 98.36% at nominal 95%.
- **Problem:** Conformal prediction's only guarantee is coverage at the nominal level; +9.5 points of over-coverage means the intervals are substantially too wide (uninformative), which is a calibration failure, not a success. Calling 85.61% "well-calibrated" against a 77% target inverts the standard. The drop to 79.05% under leak-free CV suggests the headline numbers benefit from calibration-gene leakage on a 32–33-gene panel.
- **Fix:** L235: replace "Conformal coverage remained well-calibrated at 85.61%" with "Conformal coverage for Acta2 was conservative (85.61% empirical vs. 77% nominal, +8.6 points)". In L228/L233, add the gap after 86.46% ("+9.5 points; intervals conservative, consistent with the published pipeline").  Note that coverage guarantees hold on average across genes and cells, not for each gene. Report the 10-fold CV 33-gene mean as the calibration summary, using the values in full_dataset15_cv_eval_overall_summary.json: 79.11% at 77%, 81.34% at 80%, 89.73% at 90%, 94.18% at 95%. Correct "79.05%" to 79.11%, or point to the Galaxy dataset that gives 79.05% if it differs from the local JSON.  Optionally add Acta2 CV coverage (81.17% at nominal 77%). Do not claim calibration-gene leakage without evidence.
- **Verifier:** CONFIRMED: The numbers are right. galaxy_smoke_summary.json gives empirical_coverage 0.86461 against expected_coverage 0.77 (alpha 0.23, n = 3,405), and full_dataset15_galaxy_summary.json gives 0.85609. Calling 85.61% "well-calibrated" (L235) against a 77% target is wrong wording: the coverage is 8.6 points too high, so the intervals are conservative. That part of the finding holds.  Two parts of the finder's reasoning are wrong, which is why I lower the severity to MINOR: (1) The leakage claim has no support. The cross-validated (CV) Acta2-only coverage is still 81.17% on the full dataset and 78.38% on the tutorial subset at nominal 77%. The 79.05% figure is a mean across all 33 genes, not  …

### M134. "Matched to machine precision" holds only under a pinned scikit-learn; an alternate local run in the same repo gives coverage 83.91% and r = 0.0886, and the five "replicate" runs give r = 0.1199
- **Lines:** L228, L233  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-stats  ·  **Confidence:** medium
- **Claim:** L233: "Cross-environment validation between local execution and the remote Galaxy UDT matched to machine precision ($r = 1.0000$, maximum difference $< 10^{-15}$)."
- **Evidence:** /Users/anton/git/spatTrOrbit/local_reference/smoke_acta2_summary.json: coverage 0.8391, r = 0.0886; smoke_acta2_sklearn15_summary.json: coverage 0.8649, r = 0.0861 (the value quoted in the manuscript). five_runs_summary.csv (seeds 1–5, labelled as tutorial replicates) reports coverage 0.8646 but r = 0.1199 with zero variance across seeds.
- **Problem:** The bitwise match is conditional on a specific library build; the repository itself shows that a different scikit-learn changes empirical coverage by 2.6 points, and the five-seed 'variability' experiment reports a Pearson r (0.1199) that differs from the headline tutorial r (0.0861) by 39%, implying an unreported configuration difference. Stating machine-precision agreement without these caveats overstates the reproducibility result.
- **Fix:** Name the pinned dependency versions in the UDT and Methods, report the cross-version sensitivity (0.8391 vs 0.8649 coverage) as the honest reproducibility envelope, and reconcile or explain the r = 0.1199 replicate runs.

### M135. Percent-recovery denominators shift between sections, and the VIR cluster percentages do not sum coherently
- **Lines:** L246, L252, L188, L202, L204  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-stats  ·  **Confidence:** medium
- **Claim:** L252: "Over 97.3\% of VIR proteins resided in clusters containing representatives from Indonesia, Thailand, and Peru, while lineage-unique clusters accounted for only 2\% of sequences"; Chung L188/L198 mixes 89/97 (91.8%) with 40.2–56.7% computed against a mappable subset of 91/97; Toenhake quotes 94.4–96.1% recovery on deposited peaks (L202) and 91% on rebuilt peaks (L204) for the same quantity.
- **Evidence:** 97.3% + 2% = 99.3% of sequences, leaving 0.7% unaccounted (or implying different denominators for the two statements). For Chung, 56.7% of 97 = 55 genes but 55/91 mappable = 60.4%, and the text does not state which denominator is used. For Toenhake, 'percent of published 2,118 correlated pairs' is used for both the deposited-peak arm (1,999–2,035) and the rebuilt arm (1,918) while 91.3%/96.4% in the same paragraph refer to coordinate recall and precision.
- **Problem:** Readers cannot compare the recovery figures across analyses because the denominator changes between sections without being stated; the VIR percentages are mutually inconsistent at face value.
- **Fix:** Give explicit numerators and denominators for every percentage (e.g. '55/97 published targets, or 55/91 of those with an AFUB→AFUA ortholog'), and reconcile the 97.3%/2% VIR split so the categories partition the repertoire.

## Architecture & infrastructure claims

- **Lines:** L68, L70  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** reviewer2-architecture  ·  **Confidence:** medium

### M138. Package name, Orbit/Loom naming and Pi.dev citation are inaccurate or missing

### M140. A 'community cloud' of ad-hoc tools is not supported by the UDT design, which scopes tools to the individual user

- **Claim:** L118: "Across thousands of users and hundreds of thousands of analyses, recurring patterns surface to form a community cloud of such ad-hoc tools." L285: "the community can monitor and curate an emerging tool cloud."

The Galaxy docs say endpoints 'work only on the calling user's own tools'; the only sharing is a private copy via workflow import. No user counts, analysis counts or tool-reuse statistics appear anywhere in the manuscript.
- **Problem:** This is a forward-looking vision presented in the Results as an existing mechanism. No discovery or curation pipeline exists, and 'thousands of users / hundreds of thousands of analyses' is unsourced.
- **Fix:** L118: change to the conditional, e.g. "As usage grows, recurring patterns could surface to form a community cloud of such ad-hoc tools." Either drop "thousands of users and hundreds of thousands of analyses" or cite UseGalaxy usage statistics, and state that these figures describe Galaxy as a whole, not UDTs. Add one clause noting that User-Defined Tools are currently private to their author and shared only through workflows. L285: keep the passage, but name what is still missing: admin- or registry-level cross-user indexing of UDTs, de-duplication of near-identical definitions, and a path to promote a UDT into an IUC/ToolShed wrapper.
- **Verifier:** CONFIRMED: The technical fact holds. Galaxy's UDT API is scoped per user and never adds tools to the global toolbox, so no cross-user "community cloud" of UDTs exists today. The finding overstates the framing, though. L118 opens with "Our vision for agentic science...", so it is explicitly aspirational and does not describe an existing mechanism. L285 sits in the Discussion and already reads as future work: "emerging tool cloud", "becomes an opportunity". Its premise that "tool definitions and executions are recorded in a shared environment" is literally true, because UDTs live in the server database, which admins can query across users. ### M141. 'Mapped all 42 cohort jobs concurrently across distributed high-performance nodes' is not verifiable and conflicts with queueing
- **Lines:** L260  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** gap-access-ci-compute-routing  ·  **Confidence:** medium
- **Claim:** "Galaxy mapped all 42 cohort jobs concurrently across distributed high-performance nodes."
- **Evidence:** beast-chrom/notebook.md L557: resubmission of 27_hiv1_faria2014 shows "(Queued: 80101274)". Several cohorts needed targeted resubmissions (notebook.md L551-557), and one job was OOM-killed (code 137, /jetstream2/scratch/main/jobs/80116844, in beast-chrom/activity.jsonl). UseGalaxy.org enforces per-user concurrent-job limits (https://galaxyproject.org/main). The analysis history is private (403), so the job timing cannot be checked.
- **Problem:** Mapping over a collection does not mean concurrent execution. The record shows queueing, retries and resubmissions rather than one concurrent sweep.
- **Fix:** Say 'Galaxy mapped the tool over the 42-element collection; jobs were scheduled on Jetstream2 workers, with N resubmissions'. Report wall-clock time, queue time and compute time separately.

### M142. OAuth description is imprecise: the server is its own OAuth provider that exchanges a Galaxy password for an API key
- **Lines:** L337  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** gap-mcp-endpoint-count  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** "Authentication occurs through long-lived Galaxy API keys or OAuth2 token exchanges."
- **Evidence:** v1.10.0 galaxy_mcp/auth.py: `class GalaxyOAuthProvider(OAuthProvider)` (L138) serves its own login form (L588-596). `_get_api_key` calls `{galaxy_url}api/authenticate/baseauth` with username/password (L644-648) and wraps the key in Fernet-encrypted tokens, with `exchange_authorization_code` (L260) and `exchange_refresh_token` (L323). It is HTTP-only and optional (README: "Optional OAuth login flow for HTTP deployments").
- **Problem:** Galaxy is not acting as an OAuth2 authorization server, and "token exchange" suggests RFC 8693. The real mechanism is an MCP-side OAuth 2.1 authorization-code flow backed by Galaxy basic-auth.
- **Fix:** "API keys (stdio/HTTP) or, for HTTP deployments, an optional MCP OAuth login flow that obtains a Galaxy API key via Galaxy credentials."

The GitHub repo galaxyproject/foundry exists.

### M144. gxwf validation does not check against IWC exemplars
- **Lines:** L348  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** gap-mcp-endpoint-count  ·  **Confidence:** medium
- **Claim:** "validated statically using the gxwf validation engine, which verifies graph topology, step connectivity, and tool parameter schemas against official Galaxy XML definitions and Intergalactic Workflow Commission (IWC) exemplars"
- **Evidence:** foundry/content/cli/gxwf/validate.md: "Validate Galaxy workflow structure, tool state, and optional connection compatibility", using `--tool-schema-dir` / tool cache, with `--connections` optional and `--no-tool-state` weakening it. IWC comparison is a separate Mold (content/molds/... `[[compare-against-iwc-exemplar]]`, a structural diff that guides template authoring), not part of gxwf validate. Tool schemas come from a tool cache (galaxy-tool-cache, ToolShed-derived), not directly from "official Galaxy XML".
- **Problem:** The sentence merges two separate Foundry stages. Connection checking is also optional, not always performed.
- **Fix:** Split the stages: gxwf validates structure and tool state (with optional connection checks) against cached tool schemas, and a separate Mold compares drafts with IWC exemplars.

### M156. Structural-sharing percentages are quoted inconsistently ("97.3%" vs "over 97.3%") and the complement (2%) does not close with them
- **Lines:** L246, L252  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** internal-consistency  ·  **Confidence:** medium

- **Evidence:** 97.3% + 2% = 99.3%, leaving 0.7% unaccounted; L252 additionally reports this as a result holding "across both runs" (73-cluster CPU and 76-cluster GPU branches) with a single number.

- **Fix:** Report both branches' values to one decimal place (e.g. "97.3% CPU / x% GPU") and make the residual explicit (cross-continental / two-genome / single-genome clusters summing to 100%).

## Figures, layout & LaTeX

### M157. Hype and informal phrasing
- **Lines:** L61, L66, L68, L90, L103, L179, L276, L281  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** latex-typos  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L61 "Here we build something that has never existed", "cutting-edge discovery"; L66 "adopt these agentic tools, become hooked"; L68 "equally thrilling and terrifying"; L90 "Yet beneath this biological concordance lay total computational divergence", "ephemeral debris field"; L103 "Third, and this is critical: reproducibility."; L179 "eases agents into the world of public datasets"; L276 "defining how agents should drive empirical science"; L281 "coming avalanche"
- **Evidence:** Direct quotes from the lines listed.
- **Problem:** A Nature Methods referee would see these as unsupported superlatives or anecdote. "Never existed" in particular is hard to defend given Galaxy MCP, Biomni and others (cited at L66).
- **Fix:** Remove or tone down, e.g., L61 "Here, we present a shared public plane..."; L66 drop "become hooked"; L103 "Third, reproducibility."

### M158. Subsection heading case inconsistent; ellipsis-split headings
- **Lines:** L76, L88, L101, L120, L139 vs L177-L256  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** latex-typos  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L76 "Advanced models propose vastly different analysis plans ..." / L88 "... and leave a dusty trail of intermediates" / L101 "...: The Galactic plane" (sentence case) vs L177 "Compiling a 30-Sample Fungal Transcriptomic Time-Course with Workflow Foundry" and later headings (Title Case)
- **Evidence:** The first five Results subsections use sentence case and the next eight use Title Case. Two headings form one sentence split by '...' (typed as three periods, not \ldots), and the PDF bookmarks show '... and leave a dusty trail'.
- **Problem:** Inconsistent, and not suitable for a journal: a heading should not depend on the one before it, and "dusty trail" is informal.
- **Fix:** Use sentence case throughout (Nature style), give each heading its own sentence (e.g., "Agents propose divergent analysis plans" / "Agents leave unversioned intermediates"), and lowercase "the" after the colon at L101.

- **Lines:** L472-L474  ·  **Status:** UNVERIFIED-MINOR  ·  **Auditor:** gap-visual-layout-rerun  ·  **Confidence:** high
- **Claim:** L472-L474: history, workflow and page IDs stacked with \par only and no labels.
- **Evidence:** PDF p36, Vyklická row: 'bbd44e69cb8906b59549f5524d3906f3 / ea7670a8c3fa3562 / 93fcddc692e0986f' are printed on consecutive lines with no separator or type label, so they read as a single 64-character hash. The Chung row separates IDs with commas, and the Wang row uses only URLs.

- **Fix:** Prefix each ID ('History:', 'Workflow:', 'Page:') or split them into separate rows, as Tables S4-S6 do.
